title: Release quest-cli 0.15.1 paired with lore-cli 0.15.1 (DEC-282 (a6))
description: ONE release, 0.15.1 (opum-doc DEC-282 (a6)), carrying 0.15.0 existing scope (ODOC-556, LCLI-775; see QCLI-547, held) plus the cont1 fixes gated by (a5): items 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8. 0.15.0 stays only as the 0.15.0-rc.1 release-candidate dist-tag and is never moved to latest. QCLI-571 is outside the gate: it joins 0.15.1 only if reviewed and landed before the cut, otherwise it is the first item of the patch after (QCLI-575, retargeted to 0.15.2). The version bump, tag, promotion to main and publish each wait for the leader go; registry publication is the operator own dialog (tier 3). quest promotes first (lore version-parity reads quest main package.json).

acceptanceCriteria.text: QCLI-562, QCLI-563, QCLI-568 and the item-7 close-out (QCLI-572 AC8) are landed on dev, each through a reviewed PR
The 0.15.1 version bump and CHANGELOG cut are prepared and reported to the leader before commit (DEC-182 release path)
Promotion, tag and publish happen only on the leader go; registry publication only in the operator own dialog

implementationNotes: OWED in the 0.15.1 bump PR, from DEC-282 (a10) (opum-ai/opum-doc#1866, ODOC-610): the CHANGELOG [0.15.1] gets ONE line on the lock difference, suggested wording to be fitted: "task list --across-refs: a lock waiter wait is bounded from its own start; lore 0.15.1 already resets it when the holder changes, and quest matches in 0.15.2 (QCLI-578, DEC-282 (a10))." Also from the leader: [0.15.0] was staged as an rc only and never reached latest; [0.15.1] includes 0.15.0 changes with the breaking one first (agree wording with lore-cli).

GATE ITEM (leader, 2026-11-21): QCLI-563 S5 (DEC-282 (a11): one note-prefixed stderr line, at most once per process, when the across-refs read cache fails) is wired through an injectable note sink whose default is a NO-OP. The 568 integration (Q568-INT: acrossRefsListing in main.ts creating the result-stderr sink and passing it to createAcrossRefsService) MUST connect that sink BEFORE the 0.15.1 bump, or DEC-282 (a11) ships unmet and the cache fails silently in production. Do not cut 0.15.1 until a test shows the cache-failure note on the real CLI stderr.

DEC-282 (a13) (opum-doc, opum-ai/opum-doc#1870, relayed by the leader 2026-11-21) chose option (A), the two-level content-addressed layout, for #763 (QCLI-563 round 5 = (A) plus S2-S5 and the nits); the rc slip to about 08:30-11:00Z Nov 22 is accepted under (a5) item 4; not chosen: the unbounded 3b824c16, gzip, a byte cap. GATE ITEMS carried on this release: (a) the Q568-INT review must confirm that concurrent COLD runs with the same inputs WAIT and REUSE rather than recompute (a cold run is still about 620 s at the 40-ref, 2,000-real-record shape); build Q568-INT so that holds and pin it with a test. (b) Q568-INT connects the DEC-282 (a11) stderr sink (the no-op default note sink of QCLI-563 S5) BEFORE the bump; the QBUMP review checks it with a test that FAILS if the sink is still the no-op. (c) The 0.15.1 CHANGELOG states the cold-run cost plainly: the first run on a repository is as slow as before, and later runs are fast.

GATE (leader, DEC-282 (a14) Q2, opum-ai/opum-doc#1873): the common-dir lock must not break a live holder by age alone. common-dir-lock.ts treats a holder older than staleAfterMs (10 min) as stale whatever its pid says, no heartbeat, and the measured cold run is 619-623 s, so a waiter breaks a healthy cold holder at about 600 s and recomputes alongside it. Invariant: a waiter never runs unlocked against a holder that is alive and making progress; it expires only against a holder with no sign of progress for staleAfterMs. PREFERRED: lore heartbeat shape; FALLBACK: staleAfterMs of at least about 1870 s (3x 623 s) plus a wait bound past it. A test pins that a live holder older than staleAfterMs is NOT broken. The leader picks heartbeat or fallback on measured cost and records which. Details, estimates and the verbatim (a14) text are on QCLI-568. Also from the same review for Q568-INT: ordered replay (record [stream, chunk]). The #763 merge commit 68c41d5b already feeds the cache-failure note into the lock sink path with one note per invocation; the gate to test remains: a cache-failure note on the real CLI stderr.

DEC-282 (a15) (opum-ai/opum-doc#1874): the lock heartbeat replaces the (a14) option split and is part of Q568-INT, and the rc estimate is about 12:30-17:00Z Nov 22. First-note-wins once-guard confirmed as conforming. QBUMP depends on the heartbeat landing, on the cache-failure note reaching real CLI stderr (a test that fails if the sink is a no-op: the S5 CLI test in #763 now asserts it after the #767 merge), and on the CHANGELOG lines owed (cold-run cost, lock-difference line, [0.15.0] was an rc only).
